title: GC in one screen
rememberThis: Value types live inline (stack or inside a heap object); reference types are heap objects plus a reference.
Gen 0 is nursery. LOH is ~85,000 bytes and is collected with gen 2, usually without compacting.
Dispose unmanaged and pooled resources yourself. Finalizers are a last-chance queue on another thread.
Kestrel microservices typically want server GC; containers should set heap hard limits rather than calling GC.Collect in request code.
bullets: Roots: stack slots, statics, GCHandles, finalizer queue.
SkiaSharp SKBitmap and similar native wrappers must be in using / await using.
Closures, boxing, string.concat, and materializing LINQ are the usual gen-0 storms.
V8 is generational too, but it has no server-GC mode and no LOH threshold you tune the same way.

rows.label: SOH
rows.value: Objects under the LOH threshold, generations 0–2

rows.label: LOH
rows.value: Large arrays and objects; gen 2 collection; compact on demand or hard limit

rows.label: Workstation GC
rows.value: Desktop / small processes; one GC heap; background GC by default

rows.label: Server GC
rows.value: One heap per processor; throughput for services; default on ASP.NET Core
